newsitem.title: RUSSIA: IMF team to leave Russia without loan agreement.
newsitem.headline: IMF team to leave Russia without loan agreement.

text.p: A team from the International Monetary Fund will leave Moscow without reaching a conclusion on whether to give Russia the latest tranche of a three-year $10 billion loan, the Russian central bank said in a statement.

The statement, released on Thursday, said the IMF was worried about Russia's ability to meet its commitments on revenue and other issues. "The parties failed to reach a common opinion on a number of problems," it said.
The statement said the problems had prevented the IMF mission from reaching a conclusion on its policy towards Russia.

"Arguments arose on the temporary schedule of the realisation of the decisions taken in July and August aimed at strengthening the revenue side of the budget, as well as on interpretations of the measures adopted by the Russian government to protect the domestic alcohol market," it said.
Another issue was whether new rules on foreigners' access to Russia's government securities market corresponded to the demands of the IMF charter.
The IMF is monitoring Russia's economic performance every month to see if policies are still on track, reporting back to the IMF board, which decides whether to release the loan.
The current mission is due to leave Moscow at the end of this week.
The Washington-based organisation delayed one tranche of the loan earlier this year because of doubts over Russia's ability to meet budget plans.
Officials had said the current round of talks were difficult, largely because of massive tax evasion.
The central bank statement said the IMF was seeking additional information from Russia and the delegation would return in the first half of November.
